import Hoare.While.Syntax
namespace While

inductive Ty
| num : Ty
| bool : Ty
deriving Repr, DecidableEq

inductive WellTyped : Expr → Ty → Prop
| num : WellTyped (Expr.num _) Ty.num
| bool : WellTyped (Expr.bool _) Ty.bool
| add : ∀ e1 e2, WellTyped e1 Ty.num → WellTyped e2 Ty.num →
    WellTyped (Expr.add e1 e2) Ty.num
| sub : ∀ e1 e2, WellTyped e1 Ty.num → WellTyped e2 Ty.num →
    WellTyped (Expr.sub e1 e2) Ty.num
| mul : ∀ e1 e2, WellTyped e1 Ty.num → WellTyped e2 Ty.num →
    WellTyped (Expr.mul e1 e2) Ty.num
| eq : ∀ e1 e2 t, WellTyped e1 t → WellTyped e2 t →
    WellTyped (Expr.eq e1 e2) Ty.bool
| lt : ∀ e1 e2, WellTyped e1 Ty.num → WellTyped e2 Ty.num →
    WellTyped (Expr.lt e1 e2) Ty.bool
| gt : ∀ e1 e2, WellTyped e1 Ty.num → WellTyped e2 Ty.num →
    WellTyped (Expr.gt e1 e2) Ty.bool
| le : ∀ e1 e2, WellTyped e1 Ty.num → WellTyped e2 Ty.num →
    WellTyped (Expr.le e1 e2) Ty.bool
| ge : ∀ e1 e2, WellTyped e1 Ty.num → WellTyped e2 Ty.num →
    WellTyped (Expr.ge e1 e2) Ty.bool
| and : ∀ e1 e2, WellTyped e1 Ty.bool → WellTyped e2 Ty.bool →
    WellTyped (Expr.and e1 e2) Ty.bool
| or : ∀ e1 e2, WellTyped e1 Ty.bool → WellTyped e2 Ty.bool →
    WellTyped (Expr.or e1 e2) Ty.bool

theorem WellTyped.unique : ∀ {e t1 t2}, WellTyped e t1 → WellTyped e t2 → t1 = t2 := by
  intro e t1 t2 h1 h2
  cases h1 <;> cases h2 <;> rfl

def Expr.ty : Expr → Option Ty
  | Expr.num _ => Ty.num
  | Expr.bool _ => Ty.bool
  | Expr.add e1 e2 => if e1.ty = some .num ∧ e2.ty = some .num then some .num else none
  | Expr.sub e1 e2 => if e1.ty = some .num ∧ e2.ty = some .num then some .num else none
  | Expr.mul e1 e2 => if e1.ty = some .num ∧ e2.ty = some .num then some .num else none
  | Expr.eq e1 e2 => if e1.ty = e2.ty ∧ e1.ty.isSome then some .bool else none
  | Expr.lt e1 e2 => if e1.ty = some .num ∧ e2.ty = some .num then some .bool else none
  | Expr.gt e1 e2 => if e1.ty = some .num ∧ e2.ty = some .num then some .bool else none
  | Expr.le e1 e2 => if e1.ty = some .num ∧ e2.ty = some .num then some .bool else none
  | Expr.ge e1 e2 => if e1.ty = some .num ∧ e2.ty = some .num then some .bool else none
  | Expr.and e1 e2 => if e1.ty = some .bool ∧ e2.ty = some .bool then some .bool else none
  | Expr.or e1 e2 => if e1.ty = some .bool ∧ e2.ty = some .bool then some .bool else none
  | Expr.var _ => none -- typing not supported for variables yet...

theorem WellTyped.not_eq_not_eq_ty {e1 e2 : Expr} {t1 t2 : Ty} :
  WellTyped e1 t1 → WellTyped e2 t2 → t1 ≠ t2 → ∀ t, ¬ (WellTyped (Expr.eq e1 e2) t) := by
  intro h1 h2 h3 t h4
  cases h4
  · case eq t h1' h2' =>
      have ht1 : t1 = t := WellTyped.unique h1 h1'
      have ht2 : t2 = t := WellTyped.unique h2 h2'
      rw [ht1, ht2] at h3
      contradiction

import Mathlib
import Architect
import Hoare.While.Syntax

namespace While

@[blueprint
    (statement := /-- For every pair of expressions `e1` and `e2` and every type `t'`, if the equality expression `Expr.eq e1 e2` is well typed at `t'`, then there exists a common type `u : Ty` such that both `e1` and `e2` are well typed at `u`. -/)
    (proof := /-- Invert the derivation of `WellTyped (Expr.eq e1 e2) t'`. The only constructor whose conclusion has expression `Expr.eq e1 e2` is `WellTyped.eq`; it provides a type `u : Ty`, a proof `WellTyped e1 u`, and a proof `WellTyped e2 u`. Package these two argument typings as the required existential witness. -/)]
lemma eq_welltyped_shared_type {e1 e2 : Expr} {t' : Ty} :
  WellTyped (Expr.eq e1 e2) t' → ∃ u : Ty, WellTyped e1 u ∧ WellTyped e2 u := by
  sorry_using []

@[blueprint
    (statement := /-- For every pair of expressions `e1` and `e2` and every pair of types `t` and `u`, if `e1` is well typed at `t`, `e1` is also well typed at `u`, and `e2` is well typed at `u`, then `e2` is well typed at `t`. -/)
    (proof := /-- Apply the repository theorem `WellTyped.unique` to the two derivations `WellTyped e1 t` and `WellTyped e1 u`, obtaining `t = u`. Rewrite the proof `WellTyped e2 u` along this equality to obtain `WellTyped e2 t`. -/)]
lemma shared_type_transfers_to_right_at_left_type {e1 e2 : Expr} {t u : Ty} :
  WellTyped e1 t → WellTyped e1 u → WellTyped e2 u → WellTyped e2 t := by
  sorry_using []

@[blueprint
    (statement := /-- For every pair of expressions `e1` and `e2` and all types `t` and `t'`, if `e1` is well typed at `t` and `Expr.eq e1 e2` is well typed at `t'`, then `e2` is well typed at `t`. -/)
    (proof := /-- From the equality-expression typing, use `eq_welltyped_shared_type` to obtain a common type `u` with `WellTyped e1 u` and `WellTyped e2 u`. Then use `shared_type_transfers_to_right_at_left_type` with the original proof `WellTyped e1 t` to transport the right-hand typing from `u` to `t`. -/)]
lemma eq_welltyped_yields_right_at_left_type {e1 e2 : Expr} {t t' : Ty} :
  WellTyped e1 t → WellTyped (Expr.eq e1 e2) t' → WellTyped e2 t := by
  sorry_using [eq_welltyped_shared_type, shared_type_transfers_to_right_at_left_type]

@[blueprint
    (statement := /-- For every pair of expressions `e1` and `e2` and all types `t` and `t'`, if `e1` is well typed at `t`, `e2` is not well typed at `t`, and `Expr.eq e1 e2` is well typed at `t'`, then a contradiction follows. -/)
    (proof := /-- Use `eq_welltyped_yields_right_at_left_type` on the proof `WellTyped e1 t` and the assumed typing of `Expr.eq e1 e2` to derive `WellTyped e2 t`. This contradicts the hypothesis `¬ WellTyped e2 t`. -/)]
lemma eq_welltyped_contradicts_missing_right_type {e1 e2 : Expr} {t t' : Ty} :
  WellTyped e1 t → ¬ WellTyped e2 t → WellTyped (Expr.eq e1 e2) t' → False := by
  sorry_using [eq_welltyped_yields_right_at_left_type]

@[blueprint
    (statement := /-- For every pair of expressions `e1` and `e2` and every type `t`, if `e1` is well typed at `t` and `e2` is not well typed at `t`, then for every type `t'`, the equality expression `Expr.eq e1 e2` is not well typed at `t'`. -/)
    (proof := /-- Fix an arbitrary type `t'` and assume for contradiction that `WellTyped (Expr.eq e1 e2) t'`. Applying `eq_welltyped_contradicts_missing_right_type` to the hypotheses `WellTyped e1 t`, `¬ WellTyped e2 t`, and this equality-expression typing gives `False`; therefore `¬ WellTyped (Expr.eq e1 e2) t'`. Since `t'` was arbitrary, the universal conclusion follows. -/)]
theorem WellTyped.not_welltyped_not_eq_ty {e1 e2 : Expr} {t : Ty} :
  WellTyped e1 t → ¬ WellTyped e2 t → ∀ t', ¬ (WellTyped (Expr.eq e1 e2) t') := by
  sorry_using [eq_welltyped_contradicts_missing_right_type]

end While
